beats: Anyone who had the one shared password could log into Klient — no way to tell who was really using it, or lock out just one person.
Now login goes through Google instead.
A sign-in token gets checked against an allow-list of approved emails before access is granted.
It's one shared key swapped for name badges only the right people hold.
Remove an email from the list, and that person's 30-day session is gone — everyone else keeps theirs.
